tip: To tell time say Klockan är plus the number: Klockan är tre, literally the clock is three, for it is three o'clock.
For minutes before the hour use i (to): tio i tolv means ten to twelve. i points ahead to the next hour.
For minutes after the hour use över (past): fem över åtta means five past eight.
kvart means a quarter hour in clock talk: kvart över nio is a quarter past nine.
State age with vara plus år gammal: jag är tjugofem år gammal. In everyday speech gammal is often dropped.
Definite adjective phrases double the marking: den stora bilen has den, the -a on stora, and the -en ending on bilen.
After är, adjectives match the noun. Soppan is an en-word, so varm and god take no ending.
Language names stay lowercase in Swedish: svenska, not Svenska, even elsewhere in a sentence.
Swedish has no -ing form: flyttar covers both we move and we are moving. Present tense does the job.
The -s ending can mean each other: hörs, from höra (hear), is a set phrase for we will be in touch.
Use i before a month name to mean in that month: i juni means in June.
Add -s to a verb for the passive: serverar (serves) becomes serveras (is served), no doer needed.
Particle verbs put the stress on the particle: rullar in (rolls in), where in adds the direction into.
tack means both please and thank you: nej tack declines an offer, ja tack accepts it.
Swedish splits know: vet (from veta) is knowing a fact, as in jag vet inte. Knowing a person uses känner.
The tens end in -tio, from tio (ten): sjuttio (70), åttio (80), nittio (90).
Teens 13 to 19 add -ton to the base digit: tretton (13), fjorton (14), femton (15).
sjutton (17) doubles as a mild exclamation like darn in sjutton också, besides just meaning seventeen.
